title: Plan Audience Basis
description: The audience a plan's figures are measured against: whose data, which demographic, and what population ratings and indexes are computed on. As a request input (criteria.planning_goals.audience_basis) it states the basis the buyer wants; on a plan_breakdown it states the basis the seller used, which may differ from the request. Where the request also states the target audience in targeting_overlay (demographics, audience_include), targeting_overlay governs who is targeted and this object says how that audience was counted: its demographic and audience restate the audience in the provider's notation. The measurement_source, demographic_system, demographic and reach_unit fields have the same names and meaning as on delivery-forecast.json; when a proposal carries both, they MUST agree.

measurement_source.description: Provider whose data produced the audience figures, as a lowercase slug (for example nielsen, transunion, comscore). Distinct from demographic_system, which says how the demographic is written, not whose panel or graph measured it.

demographic.description: Target demographic in the notation of demographic_system, such as A25-54.

audience.description: Signal or description selectors that define the audience when a plain demographic does not, such as behavioral segments. Same selectors as targeting_overlay.audience_include.

reach_unit.description: Unit in which reach, estimated_audience and market_audience are counted.

universe.description: Population, in reach_unit, that GRPs are rated against. When present, grps = impressions / universe * 100: one GRP is one impression per one percent of the universe, so 100 GRPs deliver one impression per member of the universe. A seller that omits it gives buyers no way to check a GRP figure and SHOULD NOT claim cross-seller comparability for it.

index_baseline.description: Population an `index` is computed against, where 100 means the audience's concentration equals that baseline's. Typical values are national and market; the label is seller-defined and buyers compare indexes only when it matches.
